react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm pathway analysis identified tryptophan metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this metabolomics dataset. Three independent enrichment methods (RaMP multi-database ORA, Mummichog m/z-direct network activity, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) converged on the same pathway with exceptional concordance: KEGG:hsa00380 / KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' scored FDR=8.86e-19 (RaMP, rank-1, 7/9 metabolites hit), p=5.41e-09 (MetaboAnalystR, rank-1, 6/9 metabolites hit), and p=0.000252 (Mummichog, rank-1, 16/17 pathway members matched via m/z network). Seven input metabolites map precisely onto canonical tryptophan catabolic branches: the serotoninergic arm (L-tryptophan → tryptamine → serotonin → melatonin) and the kynurenine/QUINolinic acid arm (L-tryptophan → 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid → quinolinic acid → NAD+). The serotonin-melatonin biosynthesis Reactome pathway (REACT:R-HSA-209931) was also significantly enriched (FDR=2.02e-08), confirming the neuroactive metabolite axis. The driver metabolites are L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), serotonin (KEGG:C00780), and quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722), which anchor both major catabolic branches. Tryptophan itself is the substrate; serotonin is the product of the aromatic amino acid decarboxylase / tryptophan hydroxylase route; quinolinic acid is the product of the indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase / kynurenine 3-monooxygenase route leading to NAD+ biosynthesis (WP:WP3645). The presence of indol-3-ylacetaldehyde (KEGG:C00637) as a shared intermediate further links the two branches. Ureidosuccinic acid (KEGG:C00438, N-carbamoyl-L-aspartic acid) and O-phosphoethanolamine (KEGG:C00346) did not map to tryptophan metabolism, indicating a secondary perturbation not captured by the convergent signal.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm pathway analysis identified tryptophan metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this metabolomics dataset. Three independent enrichment methods (RaMP multi-database ORA, Mummichog m/z-direct network activity, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) converged on the same pathway with exceptional concordance: KEGG:hsa00380 / KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' scored FDR=8.86e-19 (RaMP, rank-1, 7/9 metabolites hit), p=5.41e-09 (MetaboAnalystR, rank-1, 6/9 metabolites hit), and p=0.000252 (Mummichog, rank-1, 16/17 pathway members matched via m/z network). Seven input metabolites map precisely onto canonical tryptophan catabolic branches: the serotoninergic arm (L-tryptophan → tryptamine → serotonin → melatonin) and the kynurenine/QUINolinic acid arm (L-tryptophan → 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid → quinolinic acid → NAD+). The serotonin-melatonin biosynthesis Reactome pathway (REACT:R-HSA-209931) was also significantly enriched (FDR=2.02e-08), confirming the neuroactive metabolite axis. The driver metabolites are L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), serotonin (KEGG:C00780), and quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722), which anchor both major catabolic branches. Tryptophan itself is the substrate; serotonin is the product of the aromatic amino acid decarboxylase / tryptophan hydroxylase route; quinolinic acid is the product of the indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase / kynurenine 3-monooxygenase route leading to NAD+ biosynthesis (WP:WP3645). The presence of indol-3-ylacetaldehyde (KEGG:C00637) as a shared intermediate further links the two branches. Ureidosuccinic acid (KEGG:C00438, N-carbamoyl-L-aspartic acid) and O-phosphoethanolamine (KEGG:C00346) did not map to tryptophan metabolism, indicating a secondary perturbation not captured by the convergent signal.
